notes: Iron II wall and three rooms (8th century BCE destruction); the summit rock surface formerly thought a cult platform holds foundation cuttings of a massive building (35 x 15 m) with a rounded tower, not later than the 10th century BCE.

features.subtype: the summit was used as a quarry for large stones; two monolithic pillars 2 x 0.60 m left in place
features.period: with the Iron Age building (not later than the 10th century BCE)
features.quote: נוצל המקום כמחצבת להוצאת אבנים גדולות

title: ירושלים: הרובע היהודי 1976-1977 (Jerusalem, Jewish Quarter, eighth and ninth seasons)

notes: Israelite 'broad wall' traced 65 m; Hasmonean First Wall segment; Byzantine cardo 22.5 m wide; Hasmonean and Herodian buildings (destroyed 70 CE) under a stepped Byzantine street; Crusader hall later a Mamluk workshop with water installations; Ayyubid tower of 1212. Area 14: vaulted substructure of the Nea church with Justinian's inscription (549/550 CE).

features.subtype: drainage channels along the two colonnades
features.period: Byzantine cardo
features.quote: לאורך שני טורי העמודים היו תעלות ניקוז

title: ירושלים: חפירות לאורך חומת העיר המערבית (Jerusalem, excavations along the western city wall, final)

location_note: Between the Citadel and the south-west corner of the Old City, and south of the corner; no map reference.
notes: Hasmonean wall (probably John Hyrcanus I), Herodian additions and towers; Second Temple gate approach with stairs, breach probably by Titus repaired in the Roman period; Iron Age suburb buildings (7th century BCE); Ayyubid tower. Walls not eligible.

title: ירושלים: מבנה אופוס רטיקולטום (Jerusalem, the opus reticulatum building north-west of the Damascus Gate)

location_note: About 250 m north-west of the Damascus Gate, found by C. Schick in 1879; no map reference.
notes: Foundations of two concentric circles (33 m and 12 m across) with opus reticulatum like Herod's winter palace at Jericho; no sunken court. The excavators consider that it was a monument or mausoleum, perhaps the 'monument of the house of Herod' in Josephus; coded as a possible funerary monument (excavators' suggestion, not established). Byzantine pits.

features.subtype: round building, possibly a monument or mausoleum (excavators' suggestion)
features.period: probably Herodian; destroyed probably at the end of the Second Temple period
features.quote: שהבניין שעמד על גבי היסודות שנבדקו שימש כמצבה מפוארת

title: ירושלים: עיר דוד (Jerusalem, City of David, by Birket el-Hamra)
author: Y. Shiloh (with G. Solar, A. de Groot; A. Kloner)
location_note: Southern edge of the City of David at Birket el-Hamra, mouth of the Tyropoeon at the Kidron; bulldozer trench east of the road; no map reference.
notes: Section through a wall 3.5 m wide (Bliss and Dickie's M2 scarp) and two further walls; a dump of complete and broken vessels (cooking pots, jars, Herodian lamp, stone vessels, glass) of the second half of the 1st century BCE to the early 1st century CE covering the third wall; the second and third walls predate it and probably stood before Herod. The report restates Bliss and Dickie's plan: two parallel wall lines closing the central valley, serving as fortification and as a dam for the pools. The pottery dump is a discard deposit, not a concealed cache; not coded.

features.subtype: walls closing the outlet of the central valley (Tyropoeon), serving also as a dam for the pool system; the southern wall cut by the trench
features.period: not dated by the report (two walls predate a deposit of the late 1st century BCE - early 1st century CE)
features.quote: החוסמים את מוצא הגיא המרכזי

title: ירושלים: עיר דוד - 1978 (Jerusalem, City of David, first season)
author: Y. Shiloh
location_note: Areas A, B, D, E, G on the eastern slope of the City of David (Rothschild land); no map references.
notes: Area A: two parallel walls above Birket el-Hamra; thousands of broken 1st-century CE vessels (not later than 70 CE) against the north wall; a corner (tower?) of the Iron Age below. Area D: wall of the First Wall line (about 18 m long, 3.5 m wide) with a small gate blocked probably on the eve of the Revolt. Area E: thick wall (or retaining wall) covered by the debris of 70 CE; four Iron II building phases. Area G: Hasmonean or Herodian glacis; first clear Persian layer. Finds include lmlk, Yehud and Rhodian stamps and a monumental Hebrew inscription fragment (late 8th century BCE).

features.period: not dated
features.quote: סמוך לקבר נחשפו שתי גתות

features.subtype: one of the largest ancient quarries in the area, about 12 quarrying sites of about 40 x 30 m
features.period: not dated (Jerusalem, about 9 km away, suggested as the destination)
features.quote: מחצבה זו היא אחת המחצבות העתיקות הגדולות ביותר

title: ח'אן אל-אחמר (Khan el-Ahmar, monastery of St Euthymius)
author: Y. Meimaris
location_note: Monastery of St Euthymius at Khan el-Ahmar; no map reference.
notes: Main church floor cleared and repaired; vaulted crypt under the nave cleaned; refectory with six stone tables; storerooms destroyed in the earthquake of 659 CE; Umayyad and 12th-century finds.

features.subtype: large cistern between the main church and the cemetery
features.period: not dated separately (monastery, 5th-8th centuries CE)
features.quote: בשטח זה יש בור מים גדול

features.subtype: additional underground vaulted burial chamber north of the church prothesis, empty; burial chambers of the monastery
features.period: not dated separately (monastery)
features.quote: אותר חדר קבורה קרקעי-תת נוסף

title: הרודיון - 1978 (Lower Herodium, third season)
author: E. Netzer (with R. Bar-Nathan, R. Birger, D. Stacey)
location_note: Lower Herodium, west of the course; no map reference.
notes: Herodian ashlar hall (15 x 14 m) with niches, frescoed, reused in the Byzantine period; Herodian barrel-vaulted room; church of St Michael with baptistery and two Greek dedications.

features.subtype: silos cut into the bedrock in and outside the Herodian hall, and a built round domed silo
features.period: Byzantine
features.quote: נחפרו בתקופה הביזאנטית מספר ממגורות בתוך סלע האם

title: ח' מרצץ (Kh. el-Murassas, monastery and orchards)
author: E. Damati
screen_note: Not in the gazetteer; zoned by its map reference (Z3).
location_note: Map reference 178/133 as printed (OIG, 1 km precision).
notes: Large monastery (76 x 67 m) with a three-apsed church, mosaic-paved atrium, refectory with a marble table, annexes with a built manger; 6th-century CE Byzantine coins and lamps with crosses in a dump. Three terraced orchards with irrigation systems; the report does not date them separately.

features.subtype: cisterns visible on the surface
features.period: not dated separately (monastery, 6th-century coins)
features.quote: אטריום גדול מרוצף ברצפת פסיפס לבנה בורות מים

features.subtype: large cistern fed by two rock-cut channels (orchard 300 m east); two large cisterns at the head of the gully (southern orchard)
features.period: not dated
features.quote: בור מים גדול שהתנקזו אליו מי הגשמים בשתי תעלות

features.subtype: small high pool beside the cistern and secondary pools at lower levels
features.period: not dated
features.quote: ליד הבור בריכת מים קטנה

features.subtype: irrigation channels of U-shaped stone segments and rock-cut feeder channels
features.period: not dated
features.quote: מן הבריכה יוצאות מספר תעלות הבנויות חוליות אבן

title: מבשרת ירושלים (Mevasseret Yerushalayim, second season)
author: G. Edelstein (with H. Wikén and G. Ein Dor)
location_note: Mevasseret Yerushalayim; no map reference.
notes: Settlement of the Israelite (founded 8th-7th centuries BCE), Roman, Byzantine and Early Arab periods; wide wall perhaps a fortification; agricultural terraces up to 3 m high on the hills of Mevasseret Yerushalayim and Mevasseret Zion; study of the agricultural system with A. Horowitz and M. Kislev.

features.subtype: large winepress built of plastered stones with rock-cut channels, on the fourth terrace
features.period: basins went out of use in the Roman period; use probably began in the Israelite period
features.quote: נראה שהמתקן הוא חלק של גת גדולה

features.subtype: rock-cut water reservoir by the winepress
features.period: with the winepress area (not dated separately)
features.quote: באזור זה נמצא גם מאגר מים חצוב בסלע

features.subtype: arch-shaped dams over 3 m high in the nearby wadi creating fields
features.period: probably installed when the first settlement was founded, 8th-7th centuries BCE
features.quote: הסכרים הם דמויי קשת וגובהם עולה על 3 מ

title: ירושלים: חפירות בין שער שכם לשער החדש (Jerusalem, excavations between the Damascus Gate and the New Gate)
author: D. Tarler, A. de Groot and G. Solar
location_note: Outside the northern Old City wall between the Damascus Gate and the New Gate; no map reference.
notes: Crusader wall and rock-cut moat (about 14 m wide); Byzantine wall line under the Turkish wall; no Iron Age or Second Temple sherds. Fortifications not eligible.

title: ירושלים: הר הצופים (Jerusalem, Mount Scopus, two burial caves facing Isawiya)
author: A. Kloner
location_note: North-east part of Mount Scopus opposite Isawiya; no map reference.

features.subtype: two caves off a central courtyard: one room with six kokhim and a standing pit (ossuary, cooking pot); one room with five kokhim and a covered trough grave; doorjambs with inserted stones
features.period: end of the 1st century BCE - 1st century CE; Herodian lamp
features.quote: אשר זמנן סוף המאה הא לפסה"נ - המאה הא

title: ירושלים: מאגר מים מקומר (Jerusalem, vaulted water reservoir on the Jerusalem - Ramallah road)
author: A. Kloner (with Y. Votkin)
location_note: Between French Hill (Giv'at Shapira) and Giv'at ha-Mivtar; map reference 17226/13439 as printed.
excavated_or_surveyed: inspected (recorded); later destroyed by the contractor
notes: Reservoir 8 x 4.2 m, about 5.5 m high, ashlar barrel vault of twenty courses with draw openings, built into a pit cut in flint breccia; several plaster phases. The report suggests a fort and the Scopus of Josephus at this lookout point (suggestion only). No sherds.

features.subtype: vaulted ashlar water reservoir built in a rock-cut pit, the lower part of a vanished structure
features.period: probably Second Temple period, perhaps even Byzantine (no sherds)
features.quote: המאגר והקמרון הוקמו כנראה בימי בית שני אולי אף בתקופה הביזאנטית

title: גבעון (Gibeon, shaft tombs)
author: D. Davis
screen_note: Gibeon (el-Jib) by eye, inside the Z4 box (as HA 31-32).
location_note: Valley north-west of Gibeon; no map reference.
notes: Previously unknown MB I cemetery under silt; Roman road remains and three uninscribed milestones on the surface.

features.subtype: six burial units: four shaft tombs and two shafts only; copper daggers and spearheads
features.period: Middle Bronze Age I
features.quote: נתגלו שש יחידות קבורה כשארבע מהן היו קברי פיר

title: שכם (Shechem, Neapolis remains)
author: (staff officer for archaeology; I. el-Fani)
location_note: Arion quarter on the lower slope of Mount Gerizim; Amman Street at the foot of Mount Ebal; no map reference.
notes: Ashlar walls, cornices and arch stones attributed to the founding of Neapolis (second half of the 1st century CE); three Corinthian capitals. No feature of the eligible classes.

title: ואדי קלט (Wadi Qelt, water mill)
author: Y. Porath (aqueduct survey of the Jericho area)
screen_note: A water mill at the outlet of Wadi Qelt, not a cave report; read normally (plan section 7).
location_note: About 20 m east of Beit Jabr et-Tahtani at the outlet of Wadi Qelt into the Jericho plain; map reference 1907/1396 as printed.
notes: A 'gliding' water mill, perhaps for sugar; linked to the late aqueduct in Wadi Qelt.

features.subtype: sloping channel driving the mill, tied to the late Wadi Qelt aqueduct
features.period: probably Early Arab
features.quote: המים שהפעילו הטחנה זרמו בתעלה משופעת

title: ירושלים: הר ציון (Jerusalem, Mount Zion, old Protestant cemetery)
author: B. Pixner, D. Chen and S. Margalit
location_note: Old Protestant cemetery on Mount Zion; no map reference.
notes: Re-exposure of the gate, earthen road, drain and gate walls with tower 1 found by Bliss and Dickie (1894-1896). Four thresholds, each probably of a different period; no period named. Same campaign as phase-2 ESI02-057-mt-zion (Margalit and Pixner); same feature, not independent.

features.subtype: ancient city drainage channel inside a blocked tunnel 1.20 m under the road, running out under the gate to the Hinnom valley
features.period: not dated
features.quote: תעלת ניקוז עירונית עתיקה היוצאת מתחת לשער ומתנקזת

title: ירושלים: בית בד בארמון הנציב (Jerusalem, oil press at Armon ha-Natziv)
author: Y. Gat
location_note: Armon ha-Natziv; no map reference.
notes: The report infers a large farm or agricultural settlement here in the Mishnah and Talmud period; the press installations to be kept in a public garden.

features.subtype: oil press in a natural cave partly cut in the rock (4 x 5 m, collapsed ceiling), plastered; three cells cut in the south wall with ashlar openings; small room with a raised white mosaic surface
features.period: Byzantine sherds in the plaster; the report assumes a farm of the Mishnah and Talmud period
features.quote: טוחה טיח מעורב בחרסים ביזאנטיים

title: ירושלים: מאגר מים בצפון תלפיות (Jerusalem, water reservoir in North Talpiyot)
author: A. Kloner and Y. Gat
location_note: Caspi Street opposite no. 25, North Talpiyot; no map reference.
excavated_or_surveyed: inspected (January 1980); shaft sealed and left in place

features.subtype: plastered reservoir 7 x c. 3 m, c. 4 m high, roofed with a built vault, reached by a built shaft 2.5 m high; two plaster coats with an incised oared ship and six crosses
features.period: graffiti Byzantine; the report says the cistern may have been used earlier
features.quote: החריתות הן מהתקופה הביזאנטית אך ייתכן שהבור שימש כבר קודם
